line: *The dated and datable events of the French, in book order, merged by the main session from the phase 2 outliners' fragments (`plan/tasks/task-20261120-03-outline-french/timeline-*.md`), each line as its outliner wrote it. A date the text states is marked *(Drafted.)*; a date worked out from "le lendemain" and the like is marked *(My reading, to confirm.)* with the quote it rests on. Where the chapters give no year the outliners wrote the year as a reading, or left it open as "----"; it is not filled in here. Where the text disagrees with itself, both lines stand side by side, flagged; nothing is reconciled (R1120-33). The cross-chapter discords the outliners could not see from inside their spans are listed at the end.*
- 1865-03-25: "cinq jours après", the sea first seen (I.2 ¶56). Flagged: against the 23rd (I.1 ¶13) and the 24th (I.2 ¶57). *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- 1865-04-15, "seize jours après": the narrator's date for the crime at Washington, with the text's "vendredi saint" (I.11 ¶92). *(My reading, to confirm.)* 30 March plus sixteen days is 15 April; Good Friday of 1865 was 14 April outside the text. Flagged, not reconciled; see the report.
- 1865-03-31: "le lendemain matin", Pencroff asks where to begin; Top's collar is cut into knives; the party goes to the clay (I.13 ¶1, ¶27–¶29). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1865-03-31 and 1865-04-01: two days of brickmaking, "toute la journée et la suivante" (I.13 ¶32). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Roughly 1865-04-04 to 1865-04-05: the "deux jours qui précédèrent la cuisson" are spent gathering fuel and hunting (I.13 ¶36). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- About 1865-04-14: "cinq jours après" the pottery kiln is loaded with coal (I.13 ¶46). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- About 1865-04-20: "trois jours après" the bellows is finished (I.15 ¶30). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1865-04-20, morning: the "période métallurgique" begins; the party leaves for the ore (I.15 ¶31–¶32). *(Drafted.)*
- 1865-10-25: Pencroff begins the pirogue, "dès le lendemain" (II.1 ¶34). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1865-10-30: the exploration is set to begin "le lendemain, dès le point du jour" (II.2 ¶75). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1865-11-02: the moon is to be full "trois jours après" 30 October (II.3 ¶9). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1865-08 or later, "depuis trois mois au plus": the lead-shot incident, a shot fired on the island within three months (II.4 ¶41). *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- 1865-11-02, sunrise: the promontory; "cette journée du 2 novembre" (II.5 ¶4). *(Drafted.)* Flag: this is two days after II.3 ¶72's 31 October morning, with one day (II.4) between; the text has the 2 where the count of days gives 1 November. Both dates stand; neither is reconciled.

- The canoe is said to have been alone "pendant un jour" at the Mercy's sources (II.5 ¶12); left on 31 October, that is one day on 1 November and two on 2 November. Flag, with the date discord above. *(Drafted.)*

- 1865-11-01 to 1865-11-02, night: the colonists, finding the ladder gone, sleep badly in the Chimneys (II.6 ¶17). *(My reading, to confirm.)* The date rests on II.7 ¶9 and ¶11 (the ladder "renvoyée hier" on the morning of 3 November).
- 1865-11-21 to about 1865-12-05: the ditch dug "en moins de quinze jours" (II.7 ¶39). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1865-12-26 to 1865-12-31, "quelques jours après la capture": the cart ready, the road cut to Port Ballon (II.7 ¶61). *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- About 1866-03-09: the storm ends; the sky stays clouded to the end of summer (II.9 ¶16). *(Drafted.)* Flagged: eight days from the 2nd falls on the 10th; "vers le 9" is the text's own approximation.
- Late March 1866, undated, "à cette époque": the cycas found; flour and milk; the light cart (II.9 ¶43, ¶63). *(Drafted.)*
- 1866-08-21: Jup gets up "dix jours après avoir pris le lit" (II.12 ¶62). *(Drafted, year My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1866-10-14, about 2 p.m.: they rest under pines and plan to leave "demain au point du jour" (II.14 ¶33). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1866-10-20, 7 a.m.: the Bonadventure grounds at the Mercy's mouth. Flagged: the fire was seen at about 2 a.m. on the 19th, twenty miles off; the text says "Le lendemain" (II.15 ¶1). *(Drafted.)*
- 1866-11-04 to 1866-11-09: "Pendant les jours qui suivirent" he lives apart (II.16 ¶65). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1866-12-10: "une semaine après son retour", the request to live at the corral (II.17 ¶10). *(Drafted.)*
- About 1866-12-17: the corral house is ready "la semaine ne s’était pas écoulée" (II.17 ¶28). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- About 1853 (end): the Britannia is lost, "une année auparavant" from 20 December 1854 (II.17 ¶42); also "depuis moins de deux ans" (¶50). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1855-03 to the 1860s: Ayrton's "deux ans, trois ans", then savagery "après deux ou quatre ans" (II.17 ¶82–¶83); no dates given. *(Drafted.)*
- 1867-04-18, 8 a.m. under way; 10 a.m. the talk of the tide and the fire (II.19 ¶55, ¶69). *(My reading, to confirm: the day follows from ¶53's evening and ¶54's "ce matin-là".)*
- Discord, flagged and not reconciled: Ayrton's move to Granite-house "vers la mi-avril" (II.20 ¶73) against May's bad days (II.20 ¶71).
- 10-17, evening: the pirates have anchored a short way off; the colonists expect a landing "le lendemain" (III.2 ¶1). *(My reading, to confirm: the day is 17 October, from III.1 ¶1.)*
- 1867-12-10: improvement "dès le lendemain" (III.11 ¶10). *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 1868-02-19: the search begins "le jour même"; a week (III.13 ¶65). Discord with ¶4's "Le lendemain" (the 20th); not reconciled. *(Drafted.)*

- "Ce jour-là" (¶24), the 20th: Pencroff's approach, in the morning or day. *(My reading, to confirm.)* The day (¶46); the evening, "Till tonight, at ten o'clock" (¶44); they arrive at 9.30 p.m. (¶49); they leave that night. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶2). *(Drafted.)*
- Pencroff, "le marin" (¶3). *(Drafted.)*
- Pencroff, the sailor ("le marin"): ¶1. *(Drafted.)*
- No gun, no tool is stated; the "coup de fusil" is ruled out (¶9). *(Drafted.)*
- 26 March, dawn: "Ce matin-là, 26 mars, dès l’aube" (¶9). *(Drafted.)*
- An "îlot" off the coast (¶77). *(Drafted.)*

- Evening of 26 March, by my reading from I.6 ¶9 (the day of the hunt): ¶1 says the wind "fraîchissait avec le déclin du jour", and I.6 ¶52 has the hunters back at about six. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **The islet.** ¶77: "l’îlot, absolument invisible alors", with the definite article, as if the islet were already known. Chapter 00700's span was not given the earlier chapters; whether an islet is introduced before I.7 is for the reader of 00100 to 00300 to say. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- **Dinner and supper.** ¶21 "préparer le dîner", ¶30 "souper", ¶70 "restes du souper": same meal. *(Drafted.)*

- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Nab (¶1), Pencroff, "le marin" (¶1), Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶3), Harbert (¶3), Cyrus Smith, "l’ingénieur" (¶4; named at ¶12), Top, the dog (¶15, named by Nab; he appears in the action at ¶27).
- The Chimneys, eight miles away (¶86); "le pan coupé" before them (¶88); the islet (¶90); the granite wall (¶90).
- The storm is "de la veille" (¶90).
- **Plate captions.** The caption "Il dut s’appuyer sur le marin." is set after ¶94 but repeats words of ¶83. *(My reading, to confirm.)* It is a placement of the print, not a second event.
- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Pencroff (¶1), Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶1), Harbert (¶1), Nab (¶1), Cyrus Smith (¶14, "l’ingénieur" at ¶1 context in ¶15), Top (¶29).

- The morning: "Le lendemain, 28 mars", about eight o'clock (¶30); the hunters leave about ten (¶80); the pine nuts are found before the sun's highest point (¶97); about two o'clock (¶116); half an hour later at the bend (¶117).

- *(My reading, to confirm.)* The first evening is 27 March 1865, by "le lendemain, 28 mars"; the year rests on I.11 ¶92. The chapter covers about a day and a half, from the evening of 27 March to about 2:30 p.m. on 28 March.
- **Cyrus's lost-fire talk.** The plan to "faire des allumettes" rests on tinder or on chemistry; the text does not say how. *(Drafted.)*
- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Pencroff (¶1), Cyrus Smith (¶1), Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶1), Harbert (¶6), Nab (¶12), Top (¶18).
- The first plateau, the camp among rocks (¶44–¶45); the circular base of the upper cone (¶47); the breach, "l’égueulement" (¶51); the crater's inner slopes (¶53); the summit (¶56).
- "Le lendemain, — 29 mars" (¶18).

- *(My reading, to confirm.)* The opening scene is the afternoon of 28 March, because I.9 ¶117 puts the hunters at the river bend about 2:30 and ¶1 follows "quelques instants après". The chapter covers from about 3 p.m. on 28 March to about 8 p.m. on 29 March.

- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Cyrus Smith (¶1), Harbert (¶1), Pencroff (¶3), Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶3), Nab (¶3). Top is not named in this chapter. The narrator names Abraham Lincoln and Grant (¶89, ¶91).

- The names given: baie de l’Union, baie Washington, mont Franklin, lac Grant (¶63, ¶65); presqu’île Serpentine, promontoire du Reptile (¶66); golfe du Requin, cap Mandibule-Nord, cap Mandibule-Sud (¶68–¶71); cap de la Griffe (¶75); la Mercy, l’îlot du Salut, le plateau de Grande-Vue, les forêts du Far-West (¶78–¶81); l’île Lincoln (¶89); Les Cheminées kept (¶57).
- "Le lendemain, 30 mars" (¶2); about seven o'clock departure (¶3); before eight at the crater's top (¶9); an hour on the summit (¶34); "le 30 mars 1865" (¶92); "seize jours après" (¶92).
- The plan to fix the north "le lendemain" (¶83) is 31 March. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **The date of Lincoln's death.** ¶92 says that "seize jours après" 30 March, on Good Friday, Lincoln falls; 30 March plus sixteen days is 15 April. *(My reading, to confirm.)* Outside the text, Good Friday 1865 was 14 April and Lincoln was shot that night and died on 15 April; the chapter's count lands on the day of death, not of the shot. This is not reconciled.
- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Pencroff (¶2), Cyrus Smith (¶2), Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶2), Harbert (¶14), Nab (¶16), Top (¶13). Jonathan Forster is not in this chapter. No other person appears.
- The text calls the month "au commencement de ce mois d’avril" (¶41); see the flags. *(Drafted.)*

- **The date, "30 mars" against "commencement de ce mois d’avril".** I.11 ¶92, given to me, says "Or, ceci se passait le 30 mars 1865". This chapter ¶41 says "au commencement de ce mois d’avril, qui représente dans cet hémisphère le mois d’octobre". If this chapter is 30 March, "commencement … d’avril" is a loose phrase, or the day is 31 March or later. Card neither version. *(Drafted.)*
- The clearing, "à deux cents pas du lac Grant", on the argillaceous ground seen the day before (¶29, ¶31); the brickworks (¶38). *(Drafted.)*
- "le lendemain matin" (¶1) after the I.12 day: 31 March, if I.12 is 30 March. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Bricks: "toute la journée et la suivante" (¶32), so 31 March and 1 April. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **"quelques jours auparavant" (¶58).** Cyrus "quelques jours auparavant, saluait à la cime du mont Franklin" the Southern Cross. If the summit day was 29 or 30 March, that is about two weeks before 15 April. The text's own phrase is "quelques jours". *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Cyrus Smith (¶1), Harbert (¶4), Pencroff (¶6), Nab (¶6), Gédéon Spilett, "le reporter" (¶6), Top (not named in this chapter). Jonathan Forster and his companions are named by Pencroff (¶47); "les sudistes" (¶51).
- "Le lendemain, 16 avril, — dimanche de Pâques" (¶1). *(Drafted.)*
- Pencroff speaks of Forster finding the place bare "le lendemain matin" (¶47); the date of the balloon's escape is not given in this chapter. *(Drafted.)*
- The "énigmatique sauvetage": the place where the engineer was found remains unexplained (¶65). *(Drafted.)*
- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Pencroff (¶1), Gédéon Spilett (¶1), Cyrus Smith (¶4, "l’ingénieur"), Harbert (¶15), Nab (¶15), Top (¶33). Tubal-Cain is named as the first smith (¶42).
- "Le lendemain, 17 avril" (¶1); "La veille, après le déjeuner" the exploration to the cape (¶5), so 16 April afternoon; the night of 16 April, the decision to winter (¶5–¶6). *(Drafted.)*
- The bellows: "trois jours après" (¶30), 20 April by my count. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 20 April, dawn, the "période métallurgique" begins (¶31); the day's march through the wood; 5 p.m. halt (¶39); 8 p.m. the camp sleeps (¶40). *(Drafted.)*
- The reporter's notes: he names the period "la période métallurgique" in them (¶31). *(Drafted.)*

- **Where the ore lies: north-west or north-east.** ¶7 says the ore deposits Cyrus observed are "in the north-west part of the island"; ¶31 says the deposits are "au bas des contreforts nord-est du mont Franklin"; ¶41 "at the foot of the lateral base of one of these north-east spurs". Card neither. *(Drafted.)*
- **"Cap Mandibule", ¶5.** I.14 ¶27 and ¶38 call it "cap Mandibule-Sud"; ¶5 says "la pointe du cap Mandibule" and "les deux caps". Probably the same cape. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- **The echidna.** The summary says "Capture d’un échidné"; ¶34 describes the animal without naming it. *(Drafted.)*

- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Pencroff (¶4), Cyrus Smith (¶5), the reporter, Gédéon Spilett (¶6, named ¶11), Harbert (¶8), Nab (¶18), Top (¶29). The "indigènes" of the Malay seas and the unseen "quelque puissant animal" (¶62) are not on the page.

- The trade wind. I.16 says the east-facing coast is not exposed to the trade winds "which blow from the north-west in this hemisphere". I.19 calls the north-east winds "les mauvais vents" for the facade and speaks of "grands vents d’est" at the chimney. Card neither version. *(Drafted.)*
- The snake is "serpents-diamants ... Nouvelle-Galle du Sud" in the print's spelling (¶29). *(Drafted.)*

- **Cast.** *(Drafted.)* Cyrus Smith, Gédéon Spilett (¶1), Nab, Harbert, Pencroff (¶1). Top is not named. The narrator speaks of a "congénère des mastodontes ou autres monstres marins" (¶3), not a cast member.
- "Le lendemain, 7 mai" (¶1); the day of hauling pyrites (¶38); "Le lendemain, 8 mai" the heap is started (¶39).

- Nitro-glycerine made after that, alone (¶58–¶59); "Demain" (¶65), so the blast is on "le lendemain, — 21 mai —", dawn start (¶66); the hole finished about four in the afternoon (¶68); the explosion twenty-five minutes after the fibre is lit (¶75). The chapter covers 7 to 21 May.

- Time of day. The hole is finished "about four in the evening" on 21 May (¶68), the blast follows twenty-five minutes after the fibre is lit (¶75), yet I.18 ¶83 has the party come out of the outlet "a little before four o'clock", the same day (I.19 ¶1 opens "Le lendemain, 22 mai"). Both are quoted in the timeline. *(Drafted.)*
- Where the east bank meets the lake: "la rive est du lac Grant" (¶66) and "the part of the bank that comes nearest the coast" (¶21) are not tied together in the text. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **Time.** *(Drafted.)* The same day as the blast, 21 May *(My reading, to confirm)*: the party goes at once (¶4); the opening is widened "in less than an hour" (¶14); piercing takes two hours (¶63); they come out "a little before four o'clock" (¶83); the work is put off "au lendemain" (¶73). Top's barking a quarter of an hour before (¶54).
- The Jacamar Wood, left of the river (¶30); the Far West forests, unexplored (¶30); the warren at the "angle sud-ouest du lagon" (¶30). The view: the two Mandible capes, Cape Claw, Union Bay (¶48).

- **Time.** *(Drafted.)* "Le lendemain, 22 mai" (¶1); "quelques jours après le commencement des travaux" the facade is open (¶14); the ladder "le 28 mai" (¶28); "ce jour-là" for the warren, a day not given (¶35); "le 31 mai" partitions finished (¶43). After that, the outlet is sealed and the water brought in (¶44–¶45), with no date. The hunt "tous les jours" (¶30); a hunt of an hour's digging (¶41). The chapter covers 22 to about 31 May, and a little after. The "mauvaise saison" is near (¶30, ¶46).

- The winds. "Les mauvais vents, c’est-à-dire ceux du nord-est" (¶13) and "les grands vents d’est qui battaient directement la façade" (¶43) against I.16 ¶12, "les vents alizés, qui soufflent du nord-ouest". Card neither. *(Drafted.)*
- "Five windows and a door" for the apartment (¶4, ¶13) with a "large bay window and bull's-eye windows" for the great hall (¶13); the plan counts five compartments (¶15). *(Drafted.)*
- The date of the warren day (¶35, "ce jour-là") and of the sealing of the outlet (¶44) is not given. The sealing comes after 31 May by the text's order. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Pencroff is called "le marin" and "maître Nab" the cook (¶43), and the reporter's craft with plants (¶47) is a first sight of his taste for ornament. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **Time.** June opens winter, "which corresponds to December in the northern hemisphere" (¶1). 4 June is Whit Sunday (¶19). 5 June is the seal hunt (¶20). The candle work takes under 24 hours (¶25). "Pendant tout ce mois" the indoor work goes on (¶26). The bridges take "quelques jours" (¶29). The grain is found on an undated rainy day (¶34), and planted 20 June "le jour même" (¶66). The year is not given in the chapter; the earlier chapters put the landing in March 1865. The chapter covers about 20 days. *(Drafted.)* The 4 June Pentecost and the later Friday 30 June (I.21 ¶3) fit 1865. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- ¶20 settles that a canoe will be built "somehow or other" for the Mercy and the southwest exploration, put off "aux premiers beaux jours"; in II.1 ¶18 Pencroff proposes a canoe as if it were new: "would it not be proper, before going to explore, to build a canoe". Neither side is carded. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶4: "a serious hunt would be made for these mouflons, whose presence had been noted during the exploration of mont Frankin". The print spells "Frankin" here; elsewhere in the chapter and in I.21 it is "Franklin". Not carded. *(Drafted.)*
- **Cast.** Pencroff (¶1), Nab (¶3), Cyrus Smith (¶6), Gédéon Spilett ("le reporter", ¶10), Harbert (¶14), Top (¶8). All five colonists and the dog go on the expedition (¶8). *(Drafted.)*
- ¶16 "Chili, aux Malouines, and all those American waters crossed by the thirtieth and fortieth parallels": the island is on the thirty-fifth parallel (I.20 ¶6). *(Drafted.)*

- **Time.** Cold until 15 August (¶1); second week of August, peccaries trapped (¶14); about 15 August, wind to the northwest, snow (¶22); shut in 20 to 25 August (¶23); last week of August, the storm calms (¶29); "Vers le 25", wind to the southeast, 8 °F below zero (¶41); cold until mid-September (¶50); the cold ends, spring (¶56); second half of September, much hunting (¶57); "un mois devait s’écouler encore" before the exploration (¶60); 24 October, the trapped peccaries and the dinner at five (¶62, ¶75). The chapter covers about three and a half months. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶23 "ils restèrent renfermés pendant cinq jours, du 20 au 25 août" and ¶29 "Pendant la dernière semaine de ce mois d’août, le temps se modifia encore une fois" and ¶41 "Vers le 25, après une nouvelle alternative de neige et de pluie, le vent sauta au sud-est": the storm ends on the 25th in ¶23, and ¶41 puts a new cold, after another turn of snow and rain, at about the same day. Both quoted; not reconciled. *(Drafted.)*
- ¶21 calls the animals "des pécaris" of the "tajassous" kind; ¶14 first calls them "sangliers", and ¶14 says "sangliers qui avaient été déjà signalés au nord du lac". Both are given. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶62 "a female peccary and her two young" and ¶72 "These two little peccaries are not even three months old.": the shot in II.1 is said to have wounded "le pécari" without saying which of the two. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- ¶70 "il y a sept mois" and II.1 ¶1 "sept mois, jour pour jour": agree if the landing was 24 March (earlier chapters; not in this span). *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **Time.** "Sept mois, jour pour jour" since the landing (¶1) is the evening of 24 October. Pencroff promises the pirogue "en cinq jours au plus" (¶20). The next day work starts, the 25th (¶34). 26 October: Harbert and Spilett hunt and he climbs the kauri (¶37, ¶48). "Le surlendemain, — 28 octobre": the turtle (¶60). The turtle is left at low tide and found gone two hours later (¶74). The chapter covers four days. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶1 calls the creature in which the shot was found "a harmless rodent"; I.22 ¶62 and ¶74 have a peccary, and II.1 ¶5, ¶12 say "le pécari". A peccary is not a rodent. Both sides quoted; not reconciled. *(Drafted.)*
- ¶15 "depuis quelques semaines seulement" against ¶7 and ¶9 "depuis trois mois au plus": Cyrus's range, then his narrower guess. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶37 "it was 26 October" and ¶60 "Le surlendemain, — 28 octobre": agree. ¶34 "Dès le lendemain" puts the start on 25 October. Pencroff's five days then run to about 29 or 30 October. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Canoe built "en cinq jours" (¶1), so begun about 24 October. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- Start of the exploration set for "le lendemain, dès le point du jour" (¶75), i.e. 30 October. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- 30 October (¶1); start at six in the morning (¶8); flood began half an hour before (¶9); moon full "trois jours après" (¶9), so on 2 November by my count. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- Date of the moon: ¶9 "la lune devait être pleine trois jours après", said on 30 October, works out to 2 November. Chapter 02700 ¶4 names "cette journée du 2 novembre" for the day after the night at the Reptile promontory. See the notes for 02600 and 02700 for that discord. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- The lead shot proves a gun fired on the island "depuis trois mois au plus", ¶41. *(Drafted.)*

- Date discord to carry to 02700. This chapter is one day (6 a.m. start, night at the promontory) after the camp of 30 October, which ends "le lendemain, 31 octobre, à cinq heures du matin" (II.3 ¶72). The next chapter's morning is named "cette journée du 2 novembre" (II.5 ¶4). Nothing in this chapter or the next accounts for a day between them. Card neither version. *(Drafted.)*
- The morning is named "cette journée du 2 novembre" (¶4). *(Drafted.)*
- Cyrus Smith's lead-shot reckoning: "il y a trois mois au plus" (¶54). *(Drafted.)*
- The canoe had stayed at the Mercy's sources "pendant un jour" (¶12) and would be left "deux jours". *(Drafted.)*

- Date discord. II.3 ¶72 ends the night of 30 October: "le lendemain, 31 octobre, à cinq heures du matin, tous étaient sur pied". II.4 is one day from the falls to the promontory (6 a.m. to about 7 p.m.). This chapter then names the next day: "cette journée du 2 novembre" (¶4). A day is missing between 31 October and 2 November, or the 2 is an error for 1 November. Card neither version. *(Drafted.)*

- The date also bears on ¶12: "La pirogue est restée seule pendant un jour aux sources de la Mercy, ... elle peut bien y rester deux jours". If the canoe was left on the morning of 31 October, by the morning of 2 November it has been left two days, not one; the line fits 1 November. *(My reading, to confirm.)*
- The moon: II.3 ¶9 on 30 October says the moon will be full "trois jours après", about 2 November. *(My reading, to confirm.)*

- **Where it sits.** The French II.6, directly after II.5 ¶120 (`Il n’y avait plus d’échelle.`): the colonists, back from the west-coast excursion, find the ladder of Granite-house gone, spend the night in the Chimneys, and next day retake the dwelling from a band of apes; the chapter ends with the orang, Jup, taken into service. *(Drafted.)*

- Seam with II.5 ¶120: the last line of 02700 is `Il n’y avait plus d’échelle.` and ¶1 here opens with `Cyrus Smith s’était arrêté, sans dire mot.` and finds `l’échelle avait absolument disparu`. The first beat follows. *(Drafted.)*

- The text disagrees with itself over the ladder: ¶24 says `l’échelle inférieure avait été retirée et relevée jusqu’au seuil`, while ¶74 has the narrator say of the apes `Ils ne cherchaient même pas à replacer l’échelle, par laquelle il leur eût été facile de descendre`, and ¶42 has Pencroff say the apes climbed `par l’échelle pendant notre absence`. Card neither reading. *(Drafted.)*

- ¶101 gives the orang as `haut de six pieds`, with a `petite barbe frisée de couleur noisette`; ¶46 says Harbert declared it an orang-outang, and the narrator (¶46) is unsure between chimpanzee, orang, gorilla and gibbon. *(Drafted.)*
